newsitem.title: USA: Florida Bond Division to review Miami debt.
newsitem.headline: Florida Bond Division to review Miami debt.

text.p: A state-appointed oversight board has asked the Florida Division of Bond Finance to conduct a special review of Miami's debt, city officials said Monday.
"They're reviewing all of our outstanding bonds," city Treasurer Pete Chircut said.
The bond division will check the flow of pledged funds and the use of bond proceeds, among other things, Chircut said.
Although the division routinely reviews Florida municipalities' bonds as they are issued, the oversight board asked for a comprehensive review of the city's debt "because of Miami's situation."
Gov. Lawton Chiles appointed the oversight board in December to help Miami resolve a $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget for the year that began Oct. 1.
The city has about $590 million of bond debt oustanding, including principle and interest.
All but about $15 million is insured. Miami has not missed any debt service payments and city officials said there was no chance of a default.
